In detail

Press research on the Cabra-Glasnevin Local Electoral Area (covering Cabra, Glasnevin, and Phibsborough) found no evidence of a pervasive crime pattern or no-go areas, and one notable dated violent incident. In November 2023, two men were hospitalised with serious injuries after a stabbing at the Cabra House pub on the North Circular Road/Cabra area, following the funeral of a local man (Brandon Ledwidge); both were treated at the Mater Hospital, as reported by TheJournal.ie, RTE, and the Irish Examiner. This appears to have been an isolated, feud/funeral-related incident rather than a random attack on the public. Separately, official crime-ranking analysis (drawing on Garda station data) places the Cabra Garda district 35th of 41 Dublin Metropolitan Region districts by recorded offences in 2025 (977 offences), broadly stable since 2019 — indicating a comparatively low-crime area relative to other parts of Dublin. For Glasnevin, the main documented concern is historical: a 2018 burglary spike (30 burglaries in a three-month period, three aggravated) was raised by a local Oireachtas member and residents' policing forum, partly attributed to the 2015 closure of Whitehall Garda station; more recent (2024) Garda "Crimecall" appeals show isolated burglary investigations in Glasnevin (Dublin 9) but no evidence of a continuing spike in the 2023-2026 window. Phibsborough shows no crime-specific news coverage in this period; local news instead centres on dereliction and vacant/derelict buildings (residents' protest reported by TheJournal.ie, March 2026) and the long-delayed redevelopment of Phibsborough Shopping Centre — quality-of-life and urban-decay issues rather than safety incidents. No evidence was found of gang activity, muggings of pedestrians, or repeated violent incidents affecting residents or visitors in daytime. Given the isolated but serious nighttime stabbing and scattered burglary reports, night safety warrants a mild caution (yellow), while daytime conditions show no particular concern (green) based on available reporting. Sources checked: TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); RTE (rte.ie); Irish Examiner (irishexaminer.com); GetMyHomeReport (getmyhomereport.ie); Mary Fitzpatrick / Senator's office (maryfitzpatrick.ie); Dublin Gazette (dublingazette.com); An Garda Siochana Crimecall (garda.ie); Finglas Cabra Local Drug & Alcohol Task Force (finglascabraldtf.ie).
